x: Adam Jones was another who would have expected to place a lot higher, so in spite of a brilliant 34th from Matt Hillier, who was really flying over the last section of the race, and an equally impressive 54th from Gavin Mason, the team had to settle for 17th.

Matt Hillier and Robert Xerri of Hercules Wimbledon slug it out at Surrey League Race 4. Matt won to keep Belgrave's 100% record of individual victories but none of our high placers competed in every match, leaving the way clear for the Hercules Wimbledon lad to pick up the individual title.

Some amusement was caused by our 'B' team when M50 Tony Stone found himself being handed over to at the sharp end of the race - thanks to Messrs Sweeney and Tadesse - and further interest was added by useful performances from two of our Youths Matt Hillier and Ben Hamill.
The Under 17 trophy had more or less been expected to come our way but as the race got under way we were without our number one man Matt Hillier.

He steadily picked up eight places and was followed by Gavin Mason, who took another six, but we were just that bit too far back to do any real damage now, even with Matt Hillier setting the day's 7th fastest time on the last leg.

With much of the 'going' made up of frozen hoof prints along the horse rides of the Common, Matt Hillier later said that the jarring on his legs made him feel as if he had 'shin-splints' up to his waist.
Matt Hillier might have only got a bronze medal in the 1500m steeplechase but he relieved one of our Olympic athletes of a Club Record which has stood for over 30 years!
The Under 17s are missing Matt Hillier in the County Champs but have a scoring four right at the front. Left to right are Gavin Mason (9), Toby Earle (1), Scott Walsh, and Adam Jones (6)

The scoring ten were completed by Matt Kinnane, Owain Lewes and Matt Hillier, who had a very fine first outing in the senior race. With Alex Luce, Mike Lake, Mike Webb, Mark Anderson and Frank Ward all close behind, Belgrave would have made up for the loss at Croydon even without their stars.
○ When it came to the Guardian Gold Cup Final in September we were scratching around for steeplechasers and an unfit Matt Hillier was called into action.

It was good to see Rob Turner and Mark Sinclair running, and Matt Hillier and 1500m runner Junior Galley scored for the first time. It was, however, left to those old stagers Leo Lyons and Pete Gilbey, combined age 88 years, to complete the scoring in 114th and 115th positions.

Heading out into the country again Matt Hillier was our fourth scorer ahead of Graham Adams. Matt fell on a slippery descent, but no sympathy came from our Captain who pointedly told him to, "get up and get on with it!"
Then came Graham Adams, Jim Estall, Roger Alsop, Phil Carstairs and Matt Hillier all fairly close and swapping positions throughout the race.

On this occasion Wesley Swaffer and Matt Hillier expected to be on Southern League duty but found themselves whisked away to Linford Christie Stadium to compete in the British League.

At Reigate in the Surrey Champs. we had three Belgrave runners in the first eight in the Senior Boys' race. Matt Hillier and Adam Jones gave South Surrey a great start but it was Gavin Mason's Central Surrey team that took the winners' trophy.
